result.title: What You See Is What You Certify: Concept-Based Certificates for Unseen Compositions
result.summary: Concept-based models justify a decision by concepts they claim to see, decoded through an explicit ontology. Yet concept predictions are known to leak label information, ignore locality, and be poorly grounded on new attribute combinations. A decision decoded from such concepts can satisfy the ontology and still be wrong, so we ask when it can serve as a certificate. On unseen combinations of familiar parts, a joint concept bottleneck model and a concept embedding model, trained as is standard, certify wrong classes 93-94% of the time despite a correct ontology (60% for a joint model trained only on visible parts and gated by a localizer). The joint model's part errors copy co-occurring values more often than chance (cross-concept shortcutting). Treating the ontology as an error-detecting code, we show that a certificate needs visible evidence excluding every rival, unseen parts reported as such, and rare misreads not driven by a shared shortcut. A minimal reference design, OCVE, reads each part from a local crop in its own forward pass. On unseen FunnyBirds classes, it certifies 52% of images at 0.4% risk, against 14% for mask-pooled features and 33% for full-image part readers (5.6% when trained and gated alike), at similar zero-shot accuracy. The best baselines, even calibrated or restricted to unseen classes, and a decoder counting only agreeing parts remain about 3-8 times riskier. On CUB, isolated region readers are more accurate than an attribute-prototype model (63.1% vs. 55.3%) and certify unseen species at about 6 points less risk than it and about 10 points less than features pooled in the same keypoint boxes. On real traffic signs, isolated readers lower certified risk from 99.8% to 67%, which is still far too high; most remaining errors are misread pictograms. On seen classes the ontology brings no gain over a fairly trained black box, and isolation costs accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察概念瓶颈模型在未见部件组合上能否作为「证书」：发现标准训练的联合概念模型与概念嵌入模型在正确本体下仍以 93–94% 的比例认证错误类别，原因是部件读数会复制共现值形成跨概念捷径，并据此提出每个部件单独裁剪、独立前向读取的最小参考设计 OCVE。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「部件级证据是否真正被使用、证据是否足以排除竞争类别」的诊断与 LVR 关注的视觉细节保留、答案是否依赖视觉内容高度吻合，跨概念捷径与隔离读取的对比可供核查 latent 状态中视觉证据坍缩与定位性问题。
